# Example: parentElement

#### Course: JavaScript in Browser

## Example: parentElement

To achieve this, you can use the parentElement property:

```html
1<div class="container">
2<h1>Price List</h1>
3<ul id="price-list">
4    <li class="item">Milk <span>$2.50</span> <button class="update">Remove</button></li>
5    <li class="item">Bread <span>$1.50</span> <button class="update">Remove</button></li>
6    <li class="item">Toothpaste <span>$3.00</span> <button class="update">Remove</button></li>
7</ul>
8</div>
```

```css
1* {
2    margin: 0;
3    padding: 0;
4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6
7body {
8    font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
9    display: flex;
10    justify-content: center;
11    background-color: #f5f5f5;
12}
13
14.container {
15    width: 100%;
16    max-width: 400px;
17}
18
19h1 {
20    color: #1a237e;
21    font-size: 24px;
22    margin: 16px;
23}
24
25#price-list {
26    background-color: white;
27    border: 1px solid #e0e0e0;
28    border-radius: 8px;
29}
30
31.item {
32    padding: 12px;
33    font-size: 18px;
34    color: #1a237e;
35    border-top: 1px solid #ddd;
36    display: flex;
37    justify-content: space-between;
38    align-items: center;

42    border-top: none;
43}
44

46button {

48    padding: 6px 12px;
49    font-size: 14px;
50    color: white;
51    background-color: #f44336;
52    border: none;
53    border-radius: 4px;
54    cursor: pointer;
55    margin-left: 16px;
56}
57
58span {
59    margin-left: auto;
60}
```

```javascript
1// Get all remove buttons
2const removeButtons = document.querySelectorAll('.update');
3
4// Add an event listener to each button
5removeButtons.forEach(button => {
6    button.addEventListener('click', () => {
7    // Get the parent <li> element
8    const item = button.parentElement; 
9    // Remove the <li> element
10    item.remove(); 
11    });
12});
```

See how you accessed the parent of the button to remove the li item. This shows you can move up the DOM tree to reach any level.
